cards.text: Israel has just been carried off into Assyria (2 Kings 17:23). Now the king of Assyria brings in people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim to replace the Israelites. Five different hometowns, all moving onto one street.

cards.question: The king of Assyria brings people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim to replace the Israelites. Where does he settle them?

answers.text: In the cities of the Medes
In Gozan by the Habor River

cards.text: They take over Samaria and move right into its towns. But at first they don't worship the LORD, so He sends lions among them, and the lions kill some of them.
So the settlers send word to the king of Assyria about the lions.

cards.question: The settlers tell the king of Assyria why the lions are killing them. What do they say?

answers.text: We don't know what the God of the land requires
Our towns don't have walls to keep them out
The land sat empty and wild for far too long

cards.text: The king of Assyria has a plan. Somebody has to go live there and teach these people the requirements of the God of the land.

cards.question: The king of Assyria wants someone to go live in Samaria and teach the settlers the requirements of the God of the land. Who does he command them to send?

answers.text: One of the priests carried off from Samaria
One of the prophets living in Judah
One of his own officials from Assyria

cards.question: One of the priests carried off from Samaria comes back to teach the settlers. True or false: He comes to live in Jerusalem.

cards.text: So the priest starts teaching them how they should worship the LORD. Problem solved, right? Ohhh, friend.

cards.question: The priest is teaching the settlers how to worship the LORD. Nevertheless, the people of each nation keep making their own ___.
The people of each nation in Samaria are making their own gods. Where do they set them up?

answers.text: In the shrines on the high places

cards.text: Each nation makes its own gods, one after another. And the Sepharvites burn their children in the fire to the gods of Sepharvaim.
Here's the twist: the new residents do worship the LORD. But that's not the whole picture.

cards.question: The new residents of Samaria worship the LORD. Who do they also appoint to serve in the shrines on the high places?
The new residents worship the LORD and serve their own gods too, following the ___ of the nations they came from.

cards.text: The writer says that still, when this was written, they are practicing their former customs. None of them worship the LORD or keep the laws He gave the descendants of Jacob, whom He named Israel.
Then the writer looks back at the covenant the LORD made with the Israelites, and what He commanded them.

cards.question: In His covenant with the Israelites, what does the LORD command them first?

answers.text: Do not ever leave the land
Do not trade with the nations

cards.question: The LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt with great power. True or false: He tells them to bow down to Him and offer sacrifices to Him.

cards.text: He tells them to always keep His laws and never forget the covenant, and then He says it again, and AGAIN: “Do not worship other gods.” Friend, when you hear the same line three times, that's the line to remember.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to worship the LORD their God. What does He promise if they do?

answers.text: He will deliver them from all their enemies
He will give them a king who rules forever
He will send them rain in every season

cards.text: But the settlers would not listen. They kept right on with their former customs.

cards.question: These nations in Samaria worship the LORD but also serve their idols. True or false: Their children and grandchildren finally break the habit.
